sentences.en: After class, I was hungry and thirsty, so I called a classmate.
I said: "I'm hungry — do you want to get food together?"
He said: "Sure, I'm hungry too — let's go to that restaurant."
We walked to the restaurant, looked at the menu, and ordered rice and a dish.
After a while, the clerk brought the dish over, and we started eating.
While eating, I said: "This is so good — I'm finally not hungry anymore."
After finishing the meal, I was still a bit thirsty, so I ordered another glass of water.

quiz.q: Why did the narrator call a classmate after class?
a: Because they were hungry and thirsty

quiz.q: What did the narrator say while eating?
a: That the restaurant was too far
That the food was very good and they weren't hungry anymore

quiz.q: What did the narrator do after finishing the meal?
a: Ordered another glass of water because still thirsty

grammar.p: 我饿了 / 我渴了 (I'm hungry / thirsty)
grammar.e: Adjective + 了 marks a new state — 饿了 means 'have become hungry' and 渴了 means 'have become thirsty.'
grammar.x: 我饿了，你渴不渴？— I'm hungry, are you thirsty?

grammar.e: Repeating a verb as V+不+V makes a yes/no question, just like 是不是 or 去不去 — 想不想 asks 'do you want to or not.'
grammar.x: 你想不想一起去吃饭？— Do you want to get food together?

grammar.p: 一边...一边... (while doing X, also doing Y)
grammar.e: 一边 + verb1 + 一边 + verb2 describes two actions happening at the same time.
grammar.x: 我一边吃一边说话。— I talked while eating.
